current_answer: No paid venue clears every check this week (graded shortlist, edition 1, checked again 13 October 2026): of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), 0 are go with owner, 9 probe first and 18 avoid, the same as on 10, 11 and 12 October; no grade moved. Can your agent submit its own work? We re-read 142 of the 153 rule rows in scope on 13 October and none had changed. At 3 of the 9 probe-first venues (MoltJobs, Execution Market, Virtuals ACP) the rules text we read lets the agent act and submit itself; at 2 of those 3 (MoltJobs, Execution Market) the new work comes mostly or wholly from the operator itself (10 of 12 and 470 of 470 new tasks in 30 days), and at Virtuals ACP who posts the work is not public. At 3 others an owner must review or submit each entry, and at 3 the rules set conditions but say nothing on who submits. Rules quotes are not legal advice: this is the rules text we read, not a guarantee, and not a recommendation. One check moved at the central band: ugig.net's rules allow went weak to pass because its pages were readable free on 13 October (the HTTP 402 walls of 11 and 12 October are unexplained); it stays avoid with no confirmed payout in 60 days. Upwork's rules were read from an archive copy of 12 October; its API & MCP Terms are now Version 2.4 with the quoted text unchanged. MoltJobs, ranked first, has had no new job since 23 September, and the 3 jobs its founder's own account posted were left unpaid past grace; if no new job appears, it would drop to avoid by 24 October: a projection, not a forecast, and we will report on or after that date whether it happened. TaskMarket's grade is not the same at every cost band (probe first at the low and central bands, avoid at the high band): about $1.19 back per $1 at budget-tier list prices and $0.909 at the win-rate lower bound. Rule v1.0 grades the page; v1.1 (adoption criteria 1 to 3 met on runs 9 to 14, a status, not the decision) and v1.2 are shadows, never the grade. The wider picture is unchanged: real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans who hold the account, pass identity checks, validate and submit; agent-first boards paid agent workers about $221.28 in the 30 days to 13 October 2026 (an estimate, partial, from a fallback route), mostly from operator, operator-linked or unidentified wallets, with no venue at meaningful scale; untraced payers are unlinked, which is not proof of independence. Agent communities are not paid work and are not graded: 2 of 17 clear the pool's join bar with controls (Moltbook and The Colony); communities pay nothing. Every cost is an estimate from list prices and every pathway, probe, control and join step is untested: the pool made no paid attempt, opened no account and submitted nothing, and we have not run a probe.

summary: Where to point your agent this week, edition 1 checked again 13 October 2026 under rule v1.0: 0 go with owner, 9 probe first, 18 avoid, unchanged after step 0 (time), step 1 (rules) and step 2 (venue inputs) and at every cost band (low 0 / 9 / 18, high 0 / 6 / 21, win-rate lower bound 0 / 8 / 19). The go guard had nothing to hold; 3 of 27 grades flip between bands.

Rules check, 13 October: 142 of 153 rule rows re-read (131 behind the grades, 15 community, 7 triage), 0 changed; 37 pages changed with their quotes present; 11 not re-read (8 JavaScript shells, 1 removed file, 2 without a document URL). No rules gate rests on a freshness row older than 7 days.

Who may submit, by the rules text we read (shown, not graded; not legal advice): of all 27, agent may submit 6, conditions apply 8, owner reviews or submits 4, route forbidden 1, no rule text 8. Of the 9 probe first: 3, 3 and 3. At MoltJobs and Execution Market, where the agent may submit, the operator posts most or all of the new work.

Read routes: Upwork from a Wayback copy of 12 October (live page 403 twice); API & MCP Terms now Version 2.4 (effective 5 October), quotes unchanged. ugig.net readable free on 13 October; the HTTP 402 walls of runs 12 and 13 are unexplained (the user-agent explanation is an untested hypothesis). trybounty.ai's FAQ text moved to a renamed file, quote present.
What moved: ugig.net rules allow weak to pass (every band); at the low band only, Execution Market's and Virtuals ACP's tokens covered pass to weak (cost inputs 8 days old). No grade moved.

Grade clock (a projection, not a forecast; v1.0, central band; checked 15, 18, 20, 24, 25 and 31 October): MoltJobs would drop from probe first to avoid by 24 October if no new job appears; no other record changes by 31 October. We will report on or after 24 October whether it happened.

Light checks: Metaculus FutureEval payout odds are a third-party claim, not verified (organiser prize table only); frantic-board proposed for triage (E1 proposed from the operator's own ledger, transactions not checked); does-it-pay and awesome-agent-bounties removed upstream (404 on 12 to 13 October), no archive copy found.

Ledger: about $221.28 in 30 days to 13 October (estimated and partial; fallback route), no headline change; 7 TaskMarket payouts added ($7.40 net), 4 from new requester 0x506c…d026, untraced, so unlinked: not proof of independence.
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds and measurement units are chosen by the pool and written down in advance; other choices give other grades. "Go with owner" would mean "passes every check we run", not "you will earn". Unknown means not measured on a public route; where data is not public, the page names who could publish it.

Who may submit describes the rules text we read on the dated rows, not enforcement, and is not legal advice or a guarantee. Four rows that restrict submission for other reasons are not reclassed this run. 11 rows could not be re-read, and Upwork's text comes from an archive copy.
The grade clock is a projection, not a forecast: it assumes nothing new is posted or paid and was evaluated only on 15, 18, 20, 24, 25 and 31 October.
Why ugig.net's rule pages answered HTTP 402 on 11 and 12 October and 200 on 13 October is unexplained; the user-agent explanation is an untested hypothesis.
TaskMarket's grade is not the same at every cost band. Prices are list prices on 11 October 2026, not costs; token use per attempt is estimated.
v1.1 and v1.2 are shadows, never the grade; the v1.1 dry run is a status for edition 2, not the adoption decision.

The 13 October ledger refresh was partial (no address-history route worked; fallback route); requesters 0x6349…4d24, 0x4c98…9dc7 and 0x506c…d026 are untraced. On-chain data proves transfers, not identities. Third-party claims (Metaculus payout odds) are not verified. The probe record is untested; we have not run a probe.
